same_identity_review_evidence.reason: Every seat authors as the single GitHub account 'cehinds' (#434), so the distinct-account half of the review gate can never be satisfied in-session and every scheduler PR stalls at merge. The owner chose this over standing up a second identity, from an explicit option set in which this option was presented as NOT recommended.
same_identity_review_evidence.channel: owner-authenticated Claude Code session session_01JmAe3RaCR3kSdyfLfy8Lop, interactive AskUserQuestion selection
same_identity_review_evidence.scope: merge-dev only. Independence is taken from the scheduler's own seat identities instead of from GitHub: the item must carry a QA lease held by a seat other than its maker, and a QA verdict is only ever accepted against the exact candidate commit. Promotion to test/release/main, Pages, deployment, tagging and QA override remain owner-reserved and are unaffected.
same_identity_review_evidence.why_not_a_github_approval: GitHub refuses to let a pull request's author approve it, so with one shared account there is no obtainable GitHub approval to waive down to. An exception written in terms of one would read as a relaxation while stalling every merge exactly as before.
same_identity_review_evidence.residual_risk: Both the making seat and the verifying seat authenticate as the same GitHub login, so this is separation of actors rather than of credentials: whoever holds the account could drive both. What still holds: the verdict comes from a different seat under its own fenced lease, it is bound to the exact commit being merged, an item cannot return from PR_OPEN to candidacy and so cannot inherit an older verdict, the merge target is dev only, and every merge records review_independence in its MERGED_DEV event.
same_identity_review_evidence.restore_by: Setting same_identity_review_accepted to false once #434 fix 3 (a separate reviewing identity) exists.
